body: This is not enough information, please add more details on the steps to reproduce this, what is the output from the editor

I just created a brand new project, created a default Windows Export, executed the command line and Godot crashes (when you restart the project it tells you if you want to use recovery mode as it crashed, I assume it did). I don't see what I can add...
It doesn't happen for me, so there has to be some steps missing

Ok, I've found the issue: I was not calling the console executable but directly Godot executable.
I assume it's not supposed to happen that way (I think an error or warning would help, as it's a mistake that could happen to anyone).

That would be the reason indeed, the issue with lacking warnings for invalid command line arguments is tracked in:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10789

And similar, closing as this is more of a missing feature than a bug, with a lack of clearer feedback on user error

Thank you for reporting

Sorry for bugging you again but... It didn't solve everything.
As I said, Godot was crashing and the resulting executable was not working (when the project was big enough). Godot is no more crashing, but the executable is still not working.

If I call export from the editor or from the command line I gave you, the resulting executable is not the same. It is 92938 big when I call it from the editor and 95235 big when called from the command line. That's reproducible with a blank project. And with my main project, the 95235 big executable doesn't work.
So you were running with the editor executable?

I'll make it clearer:

Reproduction:
- Create a blank project.
- Set up a basic Windows export.
- Export
Result: The executable is 92938 big.

- Call the command line "Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win64_console.exe --path /test --export-release "Windows Desktop" Test.exe"
Result: The executable is 95235 big.

On top of that, it creates issue with my game, both executables run it differently (the 92938 runs it like in the editor, not the other one).

We still need some more information

Please run it `--verbose` when exporting and see what the output is, also try using `Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win64_console.exe /test/project.godot --verbose --export-release "Windows Desktop" Test.exe`, that would be the safest way to access the project itself

From these steps alone this isn't reproducible

> `Godot.exe --path ../Game --export-release "Windows Desktop" ../Game.exe`

Mighty be not directly related, but you should never export to the project folder, or any subfolder in it, use some other location as the target.

> Mighty be not directly related, but you should never export to the project folder, or any subfolder in it, use some other location as the target.

That doesn't do that, it exports it to `../Game.exe`, not `../Game/Game.exe`

This; Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win64_console.exe /test/project.godot --verbose --export-release "Windows Desktop" Test.exe
gives the error: Invalid project path specified: "../Godot/test/project.godot", aborting.

You must give the folder path, not the project file path.

Then the problem is that you're opening the wrong project, use `test/project.godot` not `/test/project.godot`, two different paths, also no you give the project file path, not the folder, when calling without `--path`

Also try to fix the errors that pop up

Also you should probably remove all the `.exe` files or add a `.gdignore` as they shouldn't be in the project

With errors removed and a proper call to the project file instead of it's folder:
